newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: France sends extra police after Guiana riots.
newsitem.headline: France sends extra police after Guiana riots.

text.p: France dispatched police reinforcements to French Guiana on Saturday after a second night of rioting in the capital Cayenne sparked by student protests at school conditions.

Shops and homes were damaged in the rioting overnight in Cayenne in which police fired teargas and chased youths hurling rocks and Molotov cocktail firebombs. Among stores looted was a sports shop whose owner said 40 rifles were taken.

"Today (police) reinforcements will be arriving and will enable us to better deal with the dilemma to protect property and lives," said Pierre Dartout, the administrator in the French overseas department on the northeastern coast of South America.
Officials declined to say how many para-military gendarmes were being sent in a bid to avert a third night of rioting. Radio reports said 80 were flying in.

"I call on parents of students to be watchful and to make sure that their children...do not go out in the streets at night," Dartout told local state-owned radio after the second consecutive night of clashes.

He had been barricaded for several hours inside the Cayenne prefecture on Thursday night by high school students who burned tyres and threw rocks in protest against poor conditions in local schools, witnesses said.
French Minister for Overseas Territories Jean-Jacques de Peretti said he was inviting a delegation of students to Paris to discuss their grievances.
But he said that the rioting was led by vandals "who have nothing to do with the problems of education and the young".

French Guiana's economy lags behind mainland France and it has an unemployment rate approaching 25 percent of the labour force, double that of the mainland. Joblessness is particularly acute among the young.
Cayenne's mayor, Jean-Claude Lafontaine, said he was particularly nervous after the looting of guns. "Most alarming, it seems that firearms stores have been robbed," he said.
On Friday, officials said millions of dollars of damage was caused to government buildings and shops during the first night of rioting.
